PC: As Ms. Pauls is your new patient and has not been followed for some time, you decide you need to go through a full history and physical to learn more about her and establish a baseline for her future care as well as further investigate this problem of abnormal uterine bleeding.

One of the most important topics that you want to discuss with her at this new patient visit is health maintenance such as the need for periodic mammograms every year to two years, tetanus shots every 10 years, and pap smears periodically based on guidelines.
CBC to assess for anemia due to constant bleeding, hCG to rule out pregnancy-related causes of bleeding, TSH due to history of hypothyroidism, and FSH to assess for her menopausal status.
Urine screen for gonorrhea and chlamydia to assess for infectious cervicitis etiology.

Wet mount performed by taking a sample of vaginal discharge and examining it under the microscope with and without KOH (necessary to see yeast) to assess for vagina infections of bacterial vaginosis, vaginal candidiasis, and trichamonas vaginalis.
Pap smear with HPV co-testing during the gynecologic examination to screen for cytology since she has not had a pap smear in many years.

Transvaginal Ultrasound to be preformed before her follow-up appointment to assess her endometrial lining and uterus for investigation of causes of bleeding especially due to abnormalities felt on bimanual examination. If a thickened endometrial lining is seen, you will consider endometrial biopsy to assess dysplasia or cancer.
